narrative.overview: The site is the contractor's own paperwork. Job files with spec sheets, a ruled scope-of-work list, a schedule board and a work order. Nothing is decoration: every surface is something a remodeling crew would actually hand a homeowner. The ground is limewash paper, the commitment colour is a deep olive that owns whole regions (the work-order field and the footer), and ink does the talking.
keyCharacteristics: Paper, olive and ink; brass appears only as a stamp.
One sans family (Bricolage Grotesque) at every size; mono only for numbers, measurements, job IDs and dates.
Sharp paper corners, ruled lines, square drawn checkboxes.
Before/after proof is the hero, not a picture of it.

rules.name: The Field Rule
rules.body: Olive commits at region scale (a whole section or footer) or at control scale (a chip, a box). Never as scattered accents on paper.

rules.name: The Brass Is a Stamp Rule
rules.body: Brass appears only where something has been officially received or signed off.

rules.name: The Measured Mono Rule
rules.body: Mono only carries numbers and measurements or the keys that label them. Never headlines, never body copy.

rules.name: The No Kicker Rule
rules.body: No eyebrow labels above headings; identifiers sit on the heading's line.

dos: Do keep the ground limewash (paper) and put objects on it as sheets (sheet).
Do use real photography for material texture; crop swatches from real photos rather than drawing textures.
Do keep motion to the authored moments: the renovation wipe, schedule bars drawing in sequence, the stamp press.
Do keep cursors to default, pointer on things that act, and text only inside typed fields.
donts: Don't add eyebrow labels, section numbers or icon-tile cards.
Don't rotate or tilt icons and marks on hover.
Don't use mono for anything that is not a number, measurement or its key.
Don't put a one-sided coloured stripe on a rounded box.
